Canonical block counting proves both rational spectra and the Fibonacci case; the finite verification files independently corroborate the predictions at stated bounds.

value.rationale: Finite threshold graphs are a classical structurally characterized graph family. The result determines the full FO^k logical quotient for every k>=2 (not only examples), establishes a sharp counting/variable hierarchy, gives canonical minimum representatives, and differentiates minimum model spectra from exact-order realizability using closed rational series; the width-two Fibonacci coefficients are a concrete natural enumerative consequence. The central insight is the nontrivial coexistence of arbitrarily deep peeling with variable-limited counts, not simply relabeling a known isomorphism enumeration.
